title: The canonical signed derived symmetry commutes with tensor shifts
statement: Let C be a Grothendieck abelian braided monoidal closed category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. With the signed derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and its canonical symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym], for every K in D(C), the natural transformation K tensor (-) to (-) tensor K commutes with all canonical integer shift comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0BYI, lemma-flip-douoble-tensor-product; Section section-symmetric-monoidal, the commutativity constraint with sign (-1)^(pq). Explicit shift sign calculation and descent along K-flat localization.

proof.text: On the summand of first degree p and shifted second degree q, the second-factor shift contributes (-1)^(pn), and the following symmetry contributes (-1)^(p(q+n)). Their product is (-1)^(pq), since their exponents differ by 2pn. The other route is the symmetry followed by the first-factor shift, which has exactly that sign. Extensionality of total complexes proves the chain-map equation.

For a K-flat first factor, transport this equation through the canonical left and right tensor localization comparisons, which commute with shifts. Their compatibility with the derived braiding is braiding_hom_mu. The localization from K-flat complexes is essentially surjective; transport the resulting natural transformation along an isomorphism to any derived object, using naturality and tensor bifunctor shift compatibility.
